formula.label: Trip-energy law (LawFinder-style symbolic regression, one formula per powertrain)

compute.notes: 7 time-boxed searches of 20 min wall each on a contended core (s1 ice/hev/bev, s2 ice/hev/bev, s3 plug-in): 0.857 CPU-h incl. constant refits on up to 30,000 train rows; sim-train bands seconds. Scoring the fronts and rungs (ladder.py, evaluate.py) took roughly another 0.5 CPU-h and is not training. One thread, nice 5.

formula.feature_engineering: Seven named trip summaries per row (lawvars.py), identical on both tracks: p / n = positive / negative wheel work per km at the tier's road load, t = minutes per km, m = mass (t), T = mean ambient C, c = start state (-1 warm, 0 unknown, +1 cold), d = km (+ dyn = dynamometer flag in the s2 search, f = plug-in charge-depleting share in s3). Table: read from EnergyNet's 151 inputs (route vector, physics vector, vehicle vector). Trace: recomputed from the trace + spec + rl with EnergyNet's own physics integrals (enet_features.py = byte copy of features.py; equal to the table to 1.2e-4 in log). Target per km e = y / d, loss = squared log error.
